I reported 3 findings on `ApiControllerBase.cs`, all at the new `catch (Exception)` block (line 30). I only had the diff, so I haven't read the rest of the file or the callers.

1. **Any unhandled exception returns 200 "completed"** (confidence ~95%). A `NullReferenceException`, `DbUpdateException`, `SqlException` or timeout now gives the client `200 {"status":"completed"}`. The client thinks an invoice was saved or paid when it wasn't. The exception is also never logged, and the exception-handling middleware and 5xx alerting never see it. This catch should be removed so unexpected errors reach the global handler as 500s. If you want a local fallback, log the exception and return a 500.

2. **Cancellation is reported as success** (confidence ~80%). `OperationCanceledException` and `TaskCanceledException` are caught too. A request that was aborted partway still returns 200. This matters only if actions pass cancellation tokens or run async code through this wrapper.

3. **Fallback payload has a different shape from a normal success** (confidence ~60%). A normal success returns the typed result from `Ok(action())`. The fallback returns `{ status = "completed" }`. A client that expects an `InvoiceDto` would deserialize it into blank or default fields and show no error. This is secondary to finding 1 and depends on the client code.
